data.title: Returns
data.text:
Unused items in original packaging can be returned within 30 days of delivery.
Used or worn items can't be returned. If a used item is defective, see the warranty policy.
To return an item, send it back using the return label from your account. The refund is issued to your original payment method once the warehouse receives it, usually within 5 business days.
Items that arrived damaged follow the damaged-items policy instead.

message.content:
Good head's-up question. Our return policy:

- **30-day window** from the day the tent is delivered.
- **It must be unused** and in the original packaging. Used or worn items can't be returned.

To set up a return, you use the return label from your account. Once the warehouse receives it, the refund goes back to your original payment method, usually within 5 business days.

The main exception: if the tent turns out to be defective (or arrived damaged), that's handled under our warranty/damaged-items policy instead, and you don't have to meet the "unused" condition for that.

Want help picking out a tent or checking stock before you order?

checks.label: no refunds or coupons beyond what the case allows
no raw JSON or tool syntax in replies
no invented product names, prices or specs

judgeQuestions.statement: The agent says returns are accepted within 30 days of delivery for unused items in original packaging, and states no condition the policy doesn't have (such as a restocking fee or free return shipping).

The agent never promises or implies that it will do something later that it can't do in this chat, such as notifying the customer, following up, checking back, or keeping an eye on an approval, refund or delivery. Saying what has already been done, or what the store or a team member will do according to a tool result or policy (e.g. 'a team member will review it, usually within one business day'), is fine.

Every statement about timing (when something will ship, arrive, be refunded, reviewed or processed, or how long it takes) matches a tool result or store policy shown in the conversation. Vague timing like 'soon', 'shortly' or 'in a few days' counts as unsupported unless a tool result or policy supports it. If the agent makes no timing claims, answer yes.
